Beneath the awning of a crumbling café, Clara huddled, her fingers wrapped tightly around a chipped porcelain cup, the warm steam curling around her face like a fleeting embrace. The rich scent of roasted coffee mingled with the earthy aroma of wet asphalt, creating a cocoon of comfort amidst the dreariness. She watched the world blur in the downpour, faces rushing by, umbrellas bobbing like colorful mushrooms sprouting in a forest of gray.

“Do you think it’ll ever stop?” a voice broke through her reverie, startling her. She turned to see a man, his dark hair plastered to his forehead, water streaming off the brim of his hat. He leaned against the wall, a smile playing on his lips, as if the rain were a shared joke.

“Not today, I think,” she replied, her voice barely rising above the patter of the rain. She offered a hesitant smile back, trying to shake off the weight of her thoughts, the nagging worry that had settled in her chest like an unwelcome guest.

He chuckled softly, shaking his head as if to dispel the gloom. “It’s like the sky is trying to wash away the last remnants of summer. Just when you think it’s done, it makes its grand exit.”

She nodded, letting his light-heartedness seep into her own mood. “Maybe it’s a good thing. A fresh start.”

“Or a reason to stay inside with a book,” he countered, his eyes sparkling with mischief. “What’s your poison? Romance or mystery?”

“Definitely mystery,” she said, surprised at how easily the conversation flowed. “Life’s too complicated for romance.”
